decision: D52 rung (2): A4 the error value, catch e, A1 the cause

lines.E1: `catch e` binds e, only when e is on the line of catch
lines.E2: in a text context the error is its message, byte for byte
lines.E3: Message() is the plain message; Code() is Ring's code of a VM error, "" for raise()
lines.E4: Span() is the file and line where it was raised; a rethrow keeps its origin
lines.E5: Cause() is the held error a raise in finally replaced, "" when nothing was held
lines.E6: the methods belong to the error: a plain string, or one made from an error, refuses them
lines.E7: haro fmt prints catch e as catch(e)

cases.why: `catch e` binds the error to e
`catch e` with a finally; cCatchError still reads the same error
a name on the line AFTER `catch` stays a statement: it does not bind
`catch err` with a comment after it binds
the shape of stzlib's recovered plugin code: `catch cError` in a function binds cError
in a text context the error is its message, byte for byte
Message() is the message, a plain string
Code() of an error the VM raised is Ring's code

cases.why: Code() of a raise() is empty
the four names are Ring names: any case reaches them
Span() is the file and the line where the error was raised
Span() of a VM error inside a called function is the line of the fault
a finally with no catch raises the held error again, and its Span is still where it began
raise(e) of an error value is a rethrow: it keeps the origin it had
a raise in finally replaces the held raise of the body, which is its cause
a raise in finally replaces the held raise of the HANDLER, which is its cause
causes chain: each finally that replaces an error holds the one before
a raise in finally on the normal path has no cause: nothing was held
an error the handler HANDLED is not a cause
a raise in finally replacing a held RETURN has no cause
a VM error in finally replaces the held raise too, and the cause is a whole error value
a return from the finally of an error path leaves its handler: 300 of them leave none armed

a finally that raises the held error again gives it no cause: a cause never points back at its own error
the four methods take no argument: given one, the error refuses as a string does
a VM error a finally raises again, uncaught, is reported as the VM error it is -- not as a raise()
